title: What’s new in 1.7: Alive
desc: IKANDY 1.7 makes every knob on the console one setting for every scene and gives presets a fresh start, turns Bass, Mid and Treble into color knobs for every scene, puts Motion on the beat’s hit, and adds Comfort mode, which holds fast flashing back for anyone who wants it.
text: user guide / what’s new in 1.7 what’s new in 1.7: alive ikandy 1.7 makes every knob on the console one setting for every scene and gives presets a fresh start, turns bass, mid and treble into color knobs for every scene, puts motion on the beat’s hit, and adds comfort mode, which holds fast flashing back for anyone who wants it. 1.7.1: pick your own name pick your own name on the welcome card, or later in setup, profile , change name . your number and author id never change. the name rules . comfort mode is now off unless you turn it on, in setup, comfort or with continue with comfort mode on at the first start. it no longer follows the windows animation setting. milkdrop .milk files import again. imported shaders lower their detail by themselves to stay smooth, and keep your own detail setting when you set one. they stay sharp in span. ikandy’s compute scenes and warpfield scenes no longer draw a black live wallpaper on pcs whose wallpaper runs in standard 8-bit color, as some amd graphics cards do. a crash fixed: ikandy no longer closes when listening to one app’s audio fails to start. the app’s engine is updated to electron 42.11.10 for stability and security fixes. one setting, every scene every knob on the console is one setting for every scene: set bass, speed or bloom once and it stays as you move between scenes. god rays and lut work the same way: one setting for every scene, off until you turn it on, and on auto the first time you do. an adjustment carries to the next scene until you click auto again. presets have been wiped, because your old ones were tuned for ikandy as it was. the preset you pick or save on a scene opens with that scene from then on, until you pick another; a small dot marks it. scenes without a preset play your own settings. how presets work . a preset saves every knob, intensity, god rays, lut, the look and motion, but not the milkdrop and warpfield scene knobs, which are one setting per engine. particles, emitter, coupling and persist are one setting shared by both. switch presets off with the switch beside the presets label and every scene opens on your own settings; your saved presets are kept for when you switch them back on. the lock and pin are gone: every knob now works the way the lock did. if you had the lock on, its values are now your settings for every scene. a preset never raises intensity when it is all the way down, where nothing reacts, whatever you load. to start over, press motion on the console and, under console knobs , press reset console settings : every knob goes back to ikandy’s defaults, and intensity, god rays, lut, the look, motion and your presets stay as they are. right click a knob to reset just that one. color on every scene bass, mid and treble are color knobs: bass warms the body of the picture, mid shifts its colors like oil on water and treble lights the edges, on every scene, with or without a look. they add color and never change how a scene moves. more on the color knobs . 0 turns that color off, 1 is the gentle default and 2 is the full effect. a color knob reads alike on dark and light scenes, on milkdrop, warpfield and hdr pictures too, and it never turns a color into red. the color knobs are pro. on the free plan every scene plays with them at their gentle default, and intensity is the knob you turn. motion on the hit motion starts with two moves on every plan: swell on the hit and a slow drift between hits, so a quiet passage still breathes. swell lands once on each main hit of the beat, never on every kick or hi-hat. on a scene with no centre object it gives the whole picture a small push that springs straight back. it no longer moves warpfield scenes: like milkdrop, they move themselves. imported shaders no longer speed up and slow down with every bass note: their pace follows the song, quicker in a drop and slower in a breakdown. with a look on, the rings of light it sends out on the beat are born at least a third of a second apart. when the picture goes to an audience (span, the output window or mirror, spout and ndi, the wallpaper, or recordings and replay), motion stays inside its standard range. the motion window opens from motion on the console and is pro and studio. every plan can switch the moves off: setup, comfort , motion moves turns swell, drift and any moves you added off and back on. scenes with no look on, the beat’s brightness punch lands on the main hits instead of on every bass note and hi-hat, so many of the scenes that come with ikandy flash far less on free, and on pro with the look set to original. seventeen ikandy scenes now light up on the beat’s hit instead of flickering with every note, so they flash far less at the default settings: techno flow, psytrance iridescent current, synthwave breathing current, prism cells, mercury pool, chrome chaotic flow, cyberpunk nebula flow, molten crust veins, chrome metaball, cyberpunk chase wireframe, synthwave breathing flow, face in clouds, organic flow, strobe monoliths, vibe lab hyperbolic bloom, synthwave ember flow and industrial ember flow. rave tunnel has left the library: it still flashed too often to keep. the ensemble is back in pilot, and cathedral of bars, attractor and luminous attractor have new card art with nothing drawn over the scene. pilot pilot no longer plays games or 3d worlds: slingshot, one small step, the 3d worlds, the luminal realm showcases and the flown 3d fractals on the ai shelf stay out of its show on every plan, and so do your own saved scenes built on them. a pool you build yourself, such as favorites, still plays exactly what you put in it. everything is still one click away in the library. the back arrow in pilot takes you to what pilot showed before, step by step. next and r pick the way pilot’s own switch does, so they no longer bring back something you saw a few minutes ago. a cleared luminal realm’s showcase joins your library. setup, the keys and the first launch the workspace is called setup, and its pages are audio, picture, comfort, output, keys, profile, privacy, about and debug. visual quality, highlights, the fps counter, hdr and wide gamut are together on picture. comfort mode, who is watching each output, motion moves and screen readers are on comfort, free on every plan. ui size is on output. the keys page shows pro or studio beside the keys that open a feature above your plan, and lists ctrl + shift + d , which saves a diagnostic file for support. esc closes menus and leaves span. ikandy opens about two seconds after you accept the license. the first time this version starts on your pc, now playing, lyrics, logos and pets can take up to a minute and a half to appear; after that they are there at once. comfort and flashing new: comfort mode , in setup on the comfort page under comfort and flashing. while it is on, ikandy holds back fast flashing, measured against wcag 2.3.1 and itu-r bt.1702, keeps intensity at 6 or lower and turns every motion move off. it is off until you turn it on (since 1.7.1 it no longer follows the windows animation setting). with comfort mode off, scenes play as they were made: ikandy measures their flashing but does not hold it back. milkdrop and warpfield presets play as their authors made them, and some flash or move fast. comfort mode holds them back. the photosensitivity warning at first start names comfort mode and has a continue with comfort mode on button. on the stage, flash, strobe and the return from blackout share one limit of three flashes a second, for everyone. the now playing announcement’s full-screen flash fires at most once a second, so skipping quickly through tracks no longer strobes the screen. hdr, sound and privacy picture settings live together in setup, picture : visual quality, highlights, fps counter, hdr output and headroom, wide gamut output and milkdrop per-pixel warp. hdr and 4k . on an hdr display, built-in scenes no longer look darker than on a standard screen: the shadows and midtones now match it, and only the highlights rise into hdr. when smart auto moves from your whole system’s sound to the one app playing music, the visuals keep hearing the music through the switch instead of dropping out for a moment. crash reports no longer include the title, artist or album of the song you are playing. known limits psytrance flow prime, psytrance current and vibe lab hyperbolic bloom still flash at the default settings on their own, synthwave waveform can when the look is set to original, and the one small step moon can on its first view after you start ikandy. comfort mode holds them back. comfort mode dims blocks of the picture where it holds a flash back, which shows most on bright scenes, and it lowers the frame rate. it is off unless you turn it on; click the comfort chip to turn it off. speed: the color effect adds about one millisecond a frame at 4k on an rtx 2080 ti class card. measured against 1.6.23 on the same machine, every engine runs level except milkdrop presets, which can run one step slower on very high refresh displays. this release was tested on nvidia graphics cards only; amd and intel graphics cards were not tested. the full notes, with how to use comfort mode, are in the what’s new page when you start ikandy. see pricing for what each plan includes; the steam page is authoritative. ← previous user guide next → getting started

title: Getting started
desc: Install from Steam, first launch, and the one-screen layout.
text: user guide / getting started getting started install from steam, first launch, and the one-screen layout. first launch install & first run ikandy is a windows desktop app, installed through steam. no account beyond steam, no setup wizard: you can be visualizing system audio in under a minute. install open ikandy on steam and install it like any other steam app. launch it from your steam library. steam keeps it updated automatically. ikandy opens about two seconds after you accept the license. the first time this version starts on your pc, now playing, lyrics, logos and pets can take up to a minute and a half to appear; after that they are there at once. ikandy also indexes the preset library and runs a background reactivity scan. this takes a few seconds and happens silently while you use the app. a short welcome walks you in, a one-time photosensitivity notice shows before anything flashes (it names comfort mode and lets you continue with it on), and the ? on the console replays the guided tour whenever you want it. your name your ikandy name is how other players see you on the shared moon and the name your saved shaders carry. it is your name plus a number, for example nova #12345 . new players pick a name on the welcome card. it shows large with your number beside it as you type, and the card tells you in words whether the name can be used. if you already play and still have the name ikandy made for you, ikandy asks once each time it starts until you pick one. not now waits for the next start. keep my current name appears after the first not now and ends the question for good. to change it any time, open setup , profile and press change name . the rules. 3 to 16 characters. letters, numbers, spaces and - _ . ' only. it starts and ends with a letter or a number and has at least two letters, in one alphabet. no links, emails or phone numbers, no blocked words, and no staff or ikandy names. the field tells you which rule a name breaks as you type. how often. a name ikandy made for you can be replaced at any time. after you pick your own, you can change it again 30 days later. what never changes. your number and your author id stay the same whatever name you pick, and shaders you already saved keep the name they were saved under. other players. names from other players are checked by the same rules before the moon shows them. a name that does not pass shows as player and its number. what it needs windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), 8 gb ram, 2 gb of free storage, an audio output device, and a directx 12 gpu with webgpu support (nvidia gtx 900 series, amd rx 400 series, or intel uhd 600 and newer). ikandy 1.7 was tested on nvidia graphics cards only; amd and intel graphics cards were not tested. core visual playback runs locally and does not require a separate ikandy account. steam is used for installation and licensing; optional features such as provider-based ai, online metadata, and enabled diagnostics require an internet connection. details are in the privacy policy . fastest path to visuals start playing music in any app on your computer, then in ikandy pick now playing as the source. no setup, no auth: ikandy listens to whatever windows is currently playing and starts reacting immediately. the layout one screen, one console ikandy has one layout: the full screen is the stage, and a slim console bar lives at the bottom. everything routes through that bar. when you step up to performing, stage is a second surface built for the job, and the main window always shows a return button when stage has control. the console bar, left to right now playing : album art, track title, artist. click the art to open synced lyrics. the source pill under the title shows what is connected; click it to change sources. playback : play, pause, skip, volume, and a seek bar. works with spotify, musicbee, foobar2000, vlc, and system audio, subject to each source's capabilities. library + presets : pads pick the pool the stage draws from: ikandy (the glsl and webgpu scenes), artists , or milkdrop . arrows step through looks, browse opens the full library, and auto cycles on a dwell timer you set. sound + reactivity : bass, mid and treble add color from each part of the music (pro; on free every scene plays them at their gentle default). every knob is one setting for every scene. smooth eases the reaction, and the intensity fader sets the overall strength. the reactivity panel holds light-sync, fx pulse, motion warp and motion , which opens the motion window (pro and studio; swell and drift play on every plan). the god rays chip adds light shafts and the lut chip adds a color grade; each is one setting for every scene, off until you turn it on, and on auto the first time you do (the lut’s auto picks a grade for each scene). logo places your logo over the show. view + settings : fullscreen, hide the console, a knobs / sliders switch for how the board's controls render, multi-monitor output, and the gear for setup , where sources, picture, comfort, output, keys and privacy live. vibe holds how you touch the show (particle burst, mouse and drawing effects), the console's black, chrome, ultraviolet or tape theme, and the lyrics and now playing card. the ? replays the guided tour any time. chips and workspaces, not buried menus quick controls open from chips on the console: god rays, lut and motion. bigger areas open as workspaces from the rail: now, library, create, stage, output, vibe and setup (the gear), where you connect sources and set picture, comfort, output, keys, privacy and diagnostics. live level meters sit on the board itself so you can see the signal you are mixing. multi-monitor extra displays are outputs you route to. the output window can mirror the main view onto the displays you pick, each mirror with its own gain, or span one continuous canvas edge to edge across them (the titlebar hides so nothing interrupts the image). per-display checkboxes choose which monitors take part, and live wallpaper can claim any of them as a set-and-forget desktop. mirror and span are part of pro. the tour is always current the app's built-in tour (the ? on the console) walks these zones live, on your build. if this page and your console ever disagree, trust the console. next → audio sources + controls

title: Audio sources + controls
desc: Now Playing, Spotify, MusicBee, foobar2000, VLC, per-app capture with Smart Auto, shuffle, and playlists.
text: user guide / audio sources + controls audio sources + controls now playing, spotify, musicbee, foobar2000, vlc, per-app capture with smart auto, shuffle, and playlists. audio sources connect your music ikandy can connect to five source modes. each one offers a different feature set depending on what its underlying api exposes. switching between them automatically pauses the previous one. 🎵 spotify ● works out of the box · no account connection spotify plays through windows media controls, the same lane as any modern media app. press play in spotify and ikandy picks up track info, album art when the app publishes it, and the transport controls windows exposes: play, pause, and skip. per-process capture can lock the visuals onto spotify's audio alone. there is nothing to connect: no sign-in, no developer app, no keys. ikandy has no spotify account integration; it reads what spotify publishes to windows on your machine. followed an older guide? earlier builds offered a separate spotify connection with a client id setup. that integration has been removed. nothing is required from you: play in spotify and ikandy follows automatically. 🐝 musicbee ● full features · mbxhub plugin connects through the user-installed mbxhub plugin. ikandy can read now-playing metadata and artwork, control playback, browse playlists, search, and use musicbee's shuffle and repeat modes. one-time setup download mbxhub from the official musicbee add-on page . extract the download and copy mb_mbxhub.dll and mbxhub.exe into musicbee's plugins folder. restart musicbee, then confirm mbxhub appears under edit → preferences → plugins . in ikandy, choose musicbee . leave host at 127.0.0.1 and port at 8080 unless you changed the mbxhub configuration, then click connect . connection check with musicbee and mbxhub running, open http://localhost:8080/docs . if the api documentation loads, the plugin is reachable; use the configured port if you changed it. plugin status mbxhub is published by its developer in two channels on the mbxhub download page : stable , updated about monthly and recommended for most people, and preview , updated about weekly. the plugin requires .net framework 4.8, and its companion shell requires the .net desktop runtime: .net 10 from mbxhub 0.5.5.2 on (0.5.5.1 and earlier use .net 8). if .net 10 is missing, mbxhub prompts you and helps you install it. the download page is authoritative for requirements. getting help questions about mbxhub itself (installing it, the plugin not loading, its settings) go to the mbxhub support thread on the musicbee forum . if mbxhub is running and ikandy still won't connect, see musicbee won't connect in troubleshooting. 🎧 foobar2000 ● full features · beefweb plugin for the audiophile crowd. connects via the foo_beefweb component: a rest/json api that exposes the full library. playlist browse with search, every shuffle mode foobar supports, transport, album art, lyrics. the most feature-complete source ikandy offers. one-time setup download and install foo_beefweb from github.com/hyperblast/beefweb/releases . in foobar2000: file → preferences → tools → beefweb remote control . tick enable http server (default port 8880 ). optionally set a password. click apply. in ikandy, choose foobar2000 , leave port at 8880 , enter the password if set, and click connect . foobar2000 → preferences → tools → beefweb remote control 📺 vlc ● standard · local http connects to vlc’s built-in web interface: play, pause, skip, shuffle on/off, album art, synced lyrics. no library browse; pick what to play in vlc, control playback in ikandy. one-time setup open vlc → tools → preferences . switch show settings to all . navigate to interface → main interfaces and tick web . expand main interfaces → lua , set a lua http password , and save. restart vlc. in ikandy, choose vlc , paste the password, and click connect . vlc → preferences → all → interface → main interfaces → web (ticked) custom port if port 8080 is taken, change it in the same vlc preferences pane. match it in ikandy's vlc settings. 🎙️ now playing ● basic · windows media controls · zero setup the general windows source. reads compatible apps that publish to windows media controls, including spotify, youtube music, apple music, browser tabs, and tidal. track info, available transport controls, and album art (when the app publishes it) follow the active source. no browse, no shuffle. how to use it start playing music in any app on your computer. in ikandy, click the source pill on the console and pick now playing . track info and transport light up within a second. ikandy shows or greys out individual buttons based on what the active source app actually supports. firefox needs a flag chrome and edge bridge html5 media session to windows media controls automatically. firefox doesn’t by default : open about:config , search media.hardwaremediakeys.enabled , set it to true , and restart firefox. 🎯 per-process capture ● audio isolation · setup → audio capture audio from one specific app rather than the whole system mix. if you’re gaming while listening through spotify or musicbee, ikandy normally reacts to everything: game effects, discord pings, notification sounds, and music. per-process capture can lock on to the music app alone. how to use it start the app you want to capture (for example, spotify or musicbee) and play something. in ikandy, open setup (⚙) → audio tab → what to visualize . click scan for apps . ikandy lists every app currently producing audio, with its icon. pick the app you want in the list. the banner at the top of the section confirms which app is active. to stop, click stop in the banner. ikandy returns to system audio automatically. switching apps pick a different app while one is already active : ikandy switches cleanly with no confirmation dialog. the banner updates immediately. use cases react to spotify or musicbee only, ignoring game audio and discord capture a daw or audio editor output for a live mix visualization isolate browser tab audio when youtube is playing alongside other apps test a specific app’s audio routing without affecting the rest of the system requires a connected source first per-process capture shares the same audio graph as system audio. connect a supported source (spotify, musicbee, vlc, etc.) or click 🎤 reconnect audio once before using it: this initializes the audio context. after that, per-process capture works independently. one tab runs the connections connect, disconnect, and switch available sources from ⚙ → audio : musicbee, foobar2000, vlc, spotify and other media apps through windows media controls, browser and system audio, plus the system-audio reconnect and your playlists. a source that still needs setup shows it on its row and routes you to the right place with one click. transport buttons a source cannot perform (some apps do not expose skip or seek) grey out with a hint instead of failing silently. and if you just have a file: drag an audio file onto ikandy and it plays it, no source setup at all. audio controls beyond picking a source, you shape how the audio drives the visuals. bass / mid / treble color : three color knobs (pro) that add color from each part of the music on every scene, with or without a look: bass warms the body of the picture, mid shifts its colors like oil on water and treble lights the edges. they never change how a scene moves. 0 turns that color off, 1 is the gentle default and 2 is the full effect. every knob is one setting for every scene. a smooth control eases how fast the reaction follows the music. master intensity : one fat fader for overall visual intensity on every visual, from calm to double strength. per-asset reactivity : each asset (like a logo overlay) has its own master audio-reactivity control. volume and transport : play, pause, skip, and volume for sources that support control. drop a file : drag a local audio file onto ikandy and it plays and visualizes it directly. shuffle + playlists shuffle follows the source. musicbee and foobar2000 expose their own shuffle, repeat, and playback-order modes, and the playlist panel loads supported-source playlists with search, so you can browse and play without leaving the visuals. apps that ride windows media controls, spotify included, keep their shuffle settings inside the app itself. ← previous getting started next → visualizers + presets

title: Visualizers + presets
desc: Five engines on one stage. The MilkDrop library, cycling, reactivity, and your own presets.
text: user guide / visualizers + presets visualizers + presets five engines on one stage. the milkdrop library, cycling, reactivity, and your own presets. visualizers many engines, one stage the library pads on the console pick the pool the stage draws from: ikandy , artists , or milkdrop . milkdrop is the deep preset library this page covers; the ikandy pool runs hand-built and imported scenes on glsl and webgpu, spout turns a live feed into a source, and image layers fx shaders over a photo. milkdrop, reborn milkdrop presets are rendered by warpcore, ikandy’s own milkdrop engine, which carries forward code from jordan berg’s butterchurn under its mit licence. ikandy ships a deep preset library: the base collection, extra curated packs, and an image category that layers especially well over a background photo. cycling looks auto on the console cycles presets on a dwell timer you set: how many seconds each look holds before the next. the sliders icon next to it opens timing and blend controls; a longer blend morphs cinematically between looks, a short one cuts kinetic. auto-cycle draws from a shuffle bag, so every preset in the active pool plays once before any can repeat. reactivity on first launch ikandy quietly scores the library in the background while you use the app, classifying each preset as reactive, non-reactive, or image-texture. the results are cached. in the browser, the reactive filter narrows the pool to presets that visibly answer the music; if the scan has not finished, a run scan button is right there. on milkdrop scenes the console also has a sensitivity knob: the input level beat detection hears. if the beat light misses soft passages, nudge it up; if everything slams at once, ease it back down. milkdrop presets measure the music against their own recent average, so a steady change here fades from the picture within seconds. milkdrop and warpfield presets play as their authors made them, and some flash or move fast. comfort mode holds them back. the browser browse opens the full library with thumbnails. hover any card for a live preview; click to load it on the stage immediately. scene cards preview from a cached clip the same way. tabs, favorites, hiding, flagging, and reordering are covered in library . your own presets in the browser, custom presets loads a folder of presets , merged alongside the bundled library and remembered across restarts. both formats work: classic milkdrop .milk files and butterchurn .json presets. ikandy converts .milk files itself when you pick the folder, and checks every preset before it joins your library, so there is no separate converter to run. anything that will not convert is reported rather than silently dropped. misbehaving presets some presets produce invalid values on modern gpus. ikandy skips broken or near-black presets automatically and remembers them, so the cycle keeps moving. anything questionable lands in the flagged tab for you to judge. ← previous audio sources + controls next → library: browse + manage

title: Library: browse + manage
desc: Twelve shelves, search, maker pills, favorites, hide and flag, My Scenes, previews, saving, file types.
text: user guide / library: browse + manage library: browse + manage twelve shelves, search, maker pills, favorites, hide and flag, my scenes, previews, saving, file types. one browser, twelve shelves every visual in ikandy lives in one browser, and the rail beside it groups the shelves: library (ikandy, artists, 3d worlds, game and milkdrop), mine (my scenes, workshop, images, custom and favorites), live (input and loops), and recovery , one hidden / flagged shelf for anything you set aside. the ikandy shelf holds the glsl and webgpu scenes. find it fast search filters the grid as you type, with a one-tap clear. category tabs inside milkdrop narrow the pool: all, reactive (from the reactivity scan ), your custom presets, and more. maker pills filter milkdrop by preset author with one click; glsl and webgpu get the same artist pills for their scenes. random pulls one look from the current pool and drops you straight back on the stage. three densities : list, grid, and large. large keeps cards big enough to actually read. curate it star anything : every card carries a favorite star, the favorites tab and its count update live, and shuffle can be told to draw from favorites only. hide what you never want in rotation; flag what needs a second look. both get their own tabs, so nothing is ever lost. drag to reorder : every grid in the browser reorders by drag, and your order sticks. previews hover any milkdrop card and it live-renders in a preview popup. scene cards on the visual, webgpu, and spout tabs play a cached clip on hover instead, so previews stay instant. click any card to put it on the stage immediately. my scenes scenes you compose or generate land in my scenes. each card can be replayed, renamed, or deleted. imported presets start as pending; promote the keepers into your own custom category with one action. saving, editing, versions from the studio, save as new creates a fresh asset and overwrite updates the one you are editing. originals and templates are protected: they can only be saved as new, never overwritten, and a duplicate-name guard keeps two assets from colliding. file types the image library accepts png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, and svg, and feeds both backgrounds and the logo maker . shaders paste in as glsl or wgsl text, milkdrop presets load as either classic .milk files or butterchurn .json (ikandy converts .milk itself on import, so there is no separate converter to run), and ai scenes travel as .vis packages with their provenance intact. browse music and visuals together the sync button opens the preset browser and the playlist panel as a pair, so you can line up the next track and the next look side by side. ← previous visualizers + presets next → scenes

title: Scenes
desc: The hand-built scene library and how scenes differ from presets.
text: user guide / scenes scenes the hand-built scene library and how scenes differ from presets. custom scenes audio-reactive, built in-house scenes are direct audio-reactive engines written for ikandy, driven by real-time frequency analysis. where a milkdrop preset interprets a recipe of math, a scene is code that listens: the music literally makes the picture. a library across four runtimes the scene library has grown far past its first handful, and it spans four runtimes: glsl fragment scenes, canvas2d scenes, three.js scenes, and webgpu compute scenes when your gpu supports them. the range runs from classic spectrum work (flames, bars, sweeping rays) to deep-space flythroughs, gravitational lenses, particle trails, and heavy compute pieces. flight scenes even take a game controller: plug one in and fly . turning scenes on open the library from the console and pick a scene card; it plays immediately. the intensity fader sets how hard every scene answers the audio. tone, god rays and the color grade are console settings for every scene; a scene’s own row holds only its own controls. the house rule audio drives light and color first. a scene can answer a hit with a short punch, and motion on the beat has one home, the motion window (pro and studio): swell on the hit and a slow drift are on from the start on every plan, and anything more is yours to choose. when a scene has a camera, it belongs to you or the autopilot. layering a scene and a milkdrop preset take turns on the stage rather than playing on top of each other. to stack looks, such as a base with an overlay, use mix in stage, which is part of studio. scenes and fx shaders run at the same time. make your own scenes you compose, import, or generate with ai land in my scenes , ready to replay, rename, or put in a rundown. ← previous library: browse + manage next → hdr + 4k

title: HDR + 4K
desc: True HDR on an HDR display, wide gamut on a P3 panel, and 10 bit recording. Every tier.
text: user guide / hdr + 4k hdr + 4k true hdr on an hdr display, wide gamut on a p3 panel, and 10 bit recording. every tier. light above white a normal screen stops at white. an hdr screen can go brighter than white, so a sun, a flare or a spark glows instead of flattening out. ikandy does this automatically once windows and the display are set up for it, and it tells you in plain words whether you are seeing it. set it up in windows, open settings, system, display , pick the hdr monitor and turn on use hdr . without this, windows hands ikandy a standard screen. in ikandy, open setup and the picture tab. hdr output is on by default when an hdr display is detected. read the status line under the switch: it names exactly why the current frame is or is not in hdr, and which destinations are receiving it. hdr headroom sets how far highlights may rise above white: 1.5x, 2x, 3x or 4x. 2x suits most displays. try 3x or 4x on a bright panel and step back down if it feels like too much. the cap is 4x for viewing comfort. wide gamut output turns on by itself when the display reports display p3. leave it on: the sdr show presents in p3, colors stay exact on every display, and feeds and recordings stay srgb. on a 4k display, set visual quality , on the same picture tab, to high or ultra so the gpu worlds render at the panel's native size. auto picks a tier from your gpu. hdr output and headroom apply on the next frame. turning hdr output on or off also changes the canvas format, and that part takes effect on the next launch. what stays hdr every engine finishes on one pipe. shader imports, compute worlds, milkdrop, wgsl scenes and video loops all enter the same chain, so god rays, the color grade and temporal aa look the same in hdr. supported hdr sources keep their range: pq and hlg png and avif files, jpeg gain map images, high bit depth video, windows screen capture and spout input. mirror and span map the finished frame for each display's own capability, so an hdr screen and an sdr screen beside it each get the right picture. wallpaper presents scrgb on an hdr display and a mapped sdr result elsewhere. spout offers a separate fp16 hdr sender beside the compatible sdr one. ndi output stays sdr: hdr ndi needs the separately licensed ndi advanced sdk. record in 10 bit in setup, on the output tab, under rolling replay, pick a recording dynamic range : sdr, sdr 10 bit, hdr pq or hdr hlg. sdr 10 bit writes 10 bit webm with bt.709 color from the full precision show frame, so smooth gradients keep 1024 levels instead of 256. the hdr options write 10 bit webm with bt.2020 color: pq for hdr mastering, hlg for broadcast workflows. changing the range restarts the replay buffer. if the encoder cannot do hdr, ikandy says so instead of silently writing sdr. comfort the photosensitivity warning says that hdr displays can present brighter than standard, and where the headroom control is. intensity all the way down keeps every visual calm at any headroom, and comfort mode holds fast flashing back on any display. tier note hdr output, wide gamut and 10 bit recording work at every tier, base included. the steam page is authoritative. ← previous scenes next → fx shaders

title: FX shaders
desc: Real-time post effects and the FX image pipeline.
text: user guide / fx shaders fx shaders real-time post effects and the fx image pipeline. fx real-time fx shaders fx is three layers deep in ikandy: living treatments over an image, a post chain over everything, and a play layer for your hands. fx images pick a background photo on the image engine and run a live treatment over it. the set covers weather and texture (rain, fog, heat haze, dust film), analog and broadcast decay (vhs warp, data corruption, hologram), and paint and material (ink bleed, watercolor, liquid metal, shatter, plasma arc). every treatment is audio-aware, and the library keeps growing. the post chain a multi-pass post chain runs over the whole show: bloom, chromatic aberration, grain, scanlines, vignette, and contrast, each on a live knob with its own status light, plus tone and lut color grading and a god-rays pass. beat-reactive particle bursts ride on top as their own layer. this is the finish that makes everything underneath read like one image. the play layer mouse fx and draw mode put the pointer in the show: click ripples, freehand drawing with adjustable width, and particle trails, all blended over the visuals without ever touching the camera. performance quality tiers (battery, standard, high, ultra) scale the render resolution and supersampling, so the same show runs right on a laptop on battery and on a desktop pushing a wall. ← previous hdr + 4k next → motion on the beat

title: Motion on the beat
desc: IKANDY moves every visual with your music. One Motion window holds all of it: the Look every scene gets, and your moves on the beat. It works the same way on every kind of visual, from the built-in worlds to MilkDrop presets and the shaders you import. No move ever shows past the edge of the picture, and Intensity 0 stops all of it.
text: user guide / motion on the beat motion on the beat ikandy moves every visual with your music. one motion window holds all of it: the look every scene gets, and your moves on the beat. it works the same way on every kind of visual, from the built-in worlds to milkdrop presets and the shaders you import. no move ever shows past the edge of the picture, and intensity 0 stops all of it. new in 1.7: motion starts with two moves on every plan, swell on the hit and a slow drift between hits, so a quiet passage still breathes. swell lands once on each main hit of the beat, never on every kick or hi-hat. bass, mid and treble are now color knobs for every scene. everything new in 1.7 . console, reactivity panel, motion: the motion window over the disco ball open the motion window open the dj console and find the reactivity panel. motion sits beside the light-sync, fx pulse and motion warp knobs and shows what is on: your moves (a name like swell, a count like 2 on, or off) and your look (like warp 65%). it lights up while either is on. click motion, or tab to it and press enter. the window opens at the right edge of the screen, so you can watch the picture while you tune it. the look is at the top and your moves are below it. every change applies right away and carries to every scene. press done or escape, or click outside the window, to close it. below your moves, console knobs holds reset console settings , which puts every console knob back to ikandy’s defaults. it asks first. the motion window is pro and studio. on free the motion button is locked, and swell and drift play on their own; setup, comfort , motion moves turns them off and back on. the look the musical treatment every scene gets. pick one and set its strength, from a whisper to the full effect; it starts at 65 percent. original the off switch each scene exactly as its author made it. subtle a gentle breath. bright shapes swell softly with the bass and warm a little on detail. flow bands of color travel across the picture with the music’s swell. color moves; brightness stays put. impact a ring of light bursts out from every kick and snare, tinted by the picture’s own color. warp the default on pro every kick and snare sends a ripple through the picture itself, which lights up along the wave and shimmers. nothing is drawn on top, so dark scenes stay dark. pictures, videos and games have no look, and the window says so. bass, mid and treble: color knobs the three audio knobs add color from each part of the music, on every scene, with or without a look: milkdrop, warpfield and hdr pictures included. they add color and never change how a scene moves. bass warms the body the body of the picture warms with the low end. mid shifts the colors the picture’s colors shift like oil on water. treble lights the edges the edges light up with the top end. 0 turns that color off, 1 is the gentle default and 2 is the full effect. a color knob reads alike on dark and light scenes and never turns a color into red. the color knobs are pro; on the free plan every scene plays with them at their gentle default, and intensity is the knob you turn. the moves follow the beat itself, so these knobs never stop them. the five moves each move has one amount. up to 50 percent is the standard range; above it is the wild range, up to twice as much. swell on from the start · 30% the centre object grows once on each main hit of the beat and settles, in 2d and 3d scenes alike. bounce starts at 30% the subject stretches as the beat comes, squashes on it and hops on the rebound. punch starts at 25% the whole picture pushes toward you on each hit. drift on from the start · 25% a slow glide and zoom between hits that follows the song. speaker · new starts at 30% the whole screen pumps toward you on each kick and springs back past rest, like a speaker cone. it zooms the picture in a little to leave room for the spring back. the strongest move, so start it low. swell and bounce look for a subject, such as a fractal, a disco ball or a logo, and move only that part while the rest of the frame holds still. on a scene with no centre object, swell gives the whole picture a small push that springs straight back. milkdrop presets and warpfield scenes move themselves, so swell leaves them still; bounce pulses a full-screen picture as a whole instead. add, stack, tune and remove choose add motion below your moves (it reads add more motion once a move is on). hover a move’s name to see what it does. you can stack all five. moves that move the same thing share one budget, so stacking changes the character of the motion rather than piling it higher. speaker keeps its own. up to 50 percent, the tick on the amount track, is the standard range. above it is the wild range: up to twice as much motion, with an orange readout and a note, because it can be too much for some people. it is never a default. open tune under bounce for squash (how much it flattens on the beat), hop (how high it jumps on the rebound) and focus (auto finds the subject, centre object always moves the middle, whole screen pulses the full frame). remove takes a move out. the on switch at the top of the moves turns them all off and back on without losing your settings. on the beat motion follows the beat ikandy predicts, so each hit lands on the music instead of chasing it. a build gathers, and a drop lands big. on slow songs, where a bar long rhythm could sway the whole picture, motion holds itself back. wireless headphones or a tv that plays the sound late? open setup, audio , picture timing and slide the picture later until the dot pulses with the beat you hear, or tap along and ikandy sets it for you. turning it down or off the on switch in the motion window turns the moves off and keeps your settings. intensity 0 stops all of it: every move, and the look’s reaction to the music. comfort mode turns every move off while it is on, and turning it off brings your moves back. when the picture goes to an audience (span, the output window or mirror, spout and ndi, the wallpaper, or recordings and replay), motion stays inside its standard range. if only you are watching an output, set it to personal under who is watching each output, in setup, comfort , comfort and flashing. every plan has one switch outside the console: setup, comfort , motion moves turns swell, drift and any moves you added off and back on. it is the same switch as the on switch in the motion window. while comfort mode is on it reads off and waits, because comfort mode already turns every move off. the motion window works from the keyboard (tab moves through it and escape closes it), and a screen reader hears what motion has on. the full guide is also in the app: help (f1), field guide, motion on the beat. every plan starts with the swell and drift on, and every plan has the motion moves switch in setup, comfort. the motion window is pro and studio: pro adds bounce, punch and speaker, stacking, tune and every amount, plus every look; on free, every scene plays with the look set to original. see pricing ; the steam page is authoritative. accurate as of ikandy 1.7. ← previous fx shaders next → comfort and flashing

title: Comfort and flashing
desc: IKANDY answers the music with light, and some of what plays can flash or move fast. Comfort mode holds fast flashing back for anyone who wants it. It is on every plan, Free included.
text: user guide / comfort and flashing comfort and flashing ikandy answers the music with light, and some of what plays can flash or move fast. comfort mode holds fast flashing back for anyone who wants it. it is on every plan, free included. where it lives open setup (the gear) and the comfort tab. comfort and flashing is the first card. comfort mode is off until you turn it on. choose on to turn it on and off to turn it off, and it stays the way you set it. since ikandy 1.7.1 it no longer turns on by itself when windows is set to reduce animation: only your choice turns it on. the comfort chip in the bottom left corner shows that it is on. click it to turn comfort mode off; it stays off until you turn it back on in setup. the photosensitivity warning at first start names comfort mode and has a continue with comfort mode on button. the comfort page also holds motion moves , a switch that turns every motion move off and back on without the rest of comfort mode, and screen readers , which describes each scene when it changes. everything on the comfort page is free on every plan. what it does holds back fast flashing at its strictest setting, measured against wcag 2.3.1 and itu-r bt.1702. keeps intensity at 6 or lower. turns every motion move off, whichever way it came on. your moves stay saved and come back when you turn comfort mode off. if your graphics card cannot run the flash limiter, comfort mode turns strobe, flash and the strongest looks off instead. what it costs holding a flash back has a cost you may see, which is why comfort mode is off unless you turn it on. it dims blocks of the picture where it holds a flash back, which shows most on bright scenes. a moving light can leave a short dark trail. it lowers the frame rate. who is watching each output under who is watching each output , in the same comfort and flashing section, tell ikandy how each output is watched. with comfort mode on, the closer and larger the picture is for the people watching, the smaller a flashing area has to be before comfort mode holds it back. with comfort mode on or off, when the picture goes to an audience (span, the output window or mirror, spout and ndi, the wallpaper, or recordings and replay), motion stays inside its standard range. if only you are watching an output, set it to personal . with comfort mode off scenes play as they were made: ikandy measures their flashing but does not hold it back. milkdrop and warpfield presets play as their authors made them, and some flash or move fast. comfort mode holds them back. psytrance flow prime, psytrance current and vibe lab hyperbolic bloom still flash at the default settings on their own, synthwave waveform can when the look is set to original, and the one small step moon can on its first view after you start ikandy. comfort mode holds them back. on the stage , flash, strobe and the return from blackout share one limit of three flashes a second, for everyone, with comfort mode on or off. a flash pressed too soon waits for its turn, and at very fast tempos strobe skips a beat. the now playing announcement’s full-screen flash fires at most once a second. intensity all the way down stops every reaction to the music. comfort mode is part of every plan. see pricing ; the steam page is authoritative. accurate as of ikandy 1.7. ← previous motion on the beat next → capture fx

title: Capture FX
desc: Run any app, game, window, Spout feed or video loop through effects that answer kick, snare and hats. Studio.
text: user guide / capture fx capture fx run any app, game, window, spout feed or video loop through effects that answer kick, snare and hats. studio. effects that need a feed the input tab of the library holds effects rather than standalone visuals. they run on top of video coming from somewhere else: a screen or window on this pc, a video file from your loop library, or another app such as obs, resolume, touchdesigner or madmapper. three ways in capture a screen or window. the quickest way in: point ikandy at any monitor, game or app window and the effect processes it live. native windows capture keeps hdr sources in hdr, survives a resize of the captured window, and accepts every current source. the capture toggle also lives per monitor in output stage. connect a spout sender. for a real vj rig: send a feed out of obs, resolume, touchdesigner or madmapper and receive it here at up to 60 fps. play one of your own video loops. no other app needed: add a file on the loops tab and play it, and every effect here runs on top of it. pick an effect while nothing is feeding ikandy and the app opens this same choice, the three doors plus preview anyway. the eleven capture fx time slits and time echo: time sculpture, with recorded beat ribbons and echoes of the feed. press, pixel press and glyph press: the print lab, the feed pressed into ink, pixels and glyphs. living paint and contour light: the feed's structure repainted, and traced in light. feedback cathedral, liquid glass, flow ink, and shatter and reform: retained highlights, refractive glass, source colored fluid motion, and spring driven fragments. each effect responds to kick, snare and hats with its own gestures instead of one generic pulse, and each keeps its intended color and retained state through the shared output pipeline, hdr included. the classic live-input scenes the same shelf carries the earlier spout effect scenes: live key for chroma and luma keying over a generated backdrop, datamosh, halftone, anamorphic, painterly, displace, slit scan, echo, kaleidoscope, zoom echo, glitch, pixelate, tunnel, edge, mirror, prism, liquid, dot matrix, vortex, heatwave, and original, which passes the feed through clean. good to know auto on the input shelf keeps rotating: an effect that cannot start moves on to the next. saved numbered presets, stage transitions and spout auto all work with capture fx, and switching effects repeatedly does not grow gpu memory. with a spout or ndi output attached, the show paces itself for that output at 4k instead of the console preview. tier note capture fx, screen and window capture, spout input and the video loop library ship in the studio tier, which is not on steam yet. spout output up to 30 fps is pro; see pricing . the steam page is authoritative. ← previous comfort and flashing next → spout in + out

title: Spout in + out
desc: Publish visuals to OBS and VJ software, or post-process compatible feeds.
text: user guide / spout in + out spout in + out publish visuals to obs and vj software, or post-process compatible feeds. spout a node in the rig spout is a gpu texture-sharing workflow for compatible windows apps. ikandy supports spout input and output. spout out: publish the show turn on spout output in setup, on the output tab, give the sender a name, and ikandy can appear as a source in compatible receivers such as obs, resolume, touchdesigner, madmapper, and vmix. the output is the composited visual feed; the console and panels are designed to stay out of it. output performance depends on your hardware, scene, resolution, and the receiving application. you can keep working in other apps while the feed runs. overlays on the broadcast two switches decide what rides on everything you broadcast, the second screen and spout and recordings alike: the now playing card and lyrics . one switch per overlay, so a clean feed is one click away. spout in: post-process a compatible feed pipe a live feed into ikandy from a compatible spout sender such as obs, touchdesigner, resolume, or madmapper: pick the sender in the inputs section of the output stage (output on the rail), choose a frame rate up to 60, and use the feed as a source. the library’s input shelf holds the scenes built for live feeds. tier note spout output up to 30 fps ships in the pro tier; 60 fps and above, spout input and ndi output ship in the studio tier; see pricing . the steam page is authoritative. ← previous capture fx next → wallpaper + displays

title: Wallpaper + displays
desc: Any visual behind your icons. Mirror or Span, per display, survives Explorer restarts.
text: user guide / wallpaper + displays wallpaper + displays any visual behind your icons. mirror or span, per display, survives explorer restarts. set the desktop as your stage live wallpaper runs the visual behind your desktop icons while you work, on any mix of displays, driven by whatever ikandy is listening to. it is a set-and-forget output: open output stage , click a display on the monitor map, turn on wallpaper for it, and get back to work. change the visual any time from the console or stage and the desktop follows. the wallpaper survives explorer restarts, and it keeps rendering even when the main ikandy window is covered or minimized. fit mode: mirror or span mirror (the default) puts the same feed on each screen you picked. span stretches one image across all attached displays as a single canvas; it needs two or more screens, and it takes over the routing while it is on. both modes persist. the output window separate from wallpaper, the output window is a broadcast surface: mirror the main view onto the displays you choose, each mirror with its own gain, or span one continuous visual edge to edge (the titlebar hides so nothing interrupts the image). right-click the fullscreen button for a quick "send to a second screen" chooser. add hide-ui mode and the pixels are all that is left. overlays the now playing card and lyrics each have a broadcast switch: show them on the second screen, spout, and recordings, or keep every output clean. good to know toggle wallpaper off any time from the same panel if anything misbehaves. performance cost scales with the visual you pick. calm scenes cost very little; heavy compute scenes cost more. tier note desktop wallpaper ships in the pro tier, on any number of displays and in both fit modes. the output window on a single screen is also pro. spanning one visual across multiple monitors is pro too (it moved down from studio in august 2026), and so is mirroring onto several screens at once; see pricing . the steam page is authoritative. ← previous spout in + out next → loops + recording

title: Loops + recording
desc: Your own video loops as a layer in the show, plus F9 replay, Shift+F9 recording and bar-locked loop capture.
text: user guide / loops + recording loops + recording your own video loops as a layer in the show, plus f9 replay, shift+f9 recording and bar-locked loop capture. my loops the loops tab of the library is a video library of your own files. a loop plays as a feed on the show, so every capture fx and live-input effect can run on top of it. add and play open the library and the loops tab. press add video , or drop a video anywhere in the ikandy window. mp4, webm, mov, m4v and mkv are accepted; the file is copied into your library, deduplicated, and given a cover. click a loop to play it. the library closes, the playing canvas comes forward, and the input effects go to auto. each card has a favorite and a name you can set. loops play muted: the reaction always comes from the audio source ikandy is listening to. loops do not join auto rotation on their own. a fresh install ships with one starter clip, a 30 second big buck bunny excerpt (blender foundation, cc by 3.0), so the library is never empty. hdr loops high bit depth video keeps its color and highlight range through loops, mix and the canvas, and image studio plays hdr loops natively. display p3 video keeps its gamut all the way to the screen. replay and record f9 saves the last 30 seconds. rolling replay keeps a buffer running in the background so f9 has those seconds. it is off by default because it costs some gpu, and pressing f9 turns it on for you. shift + f9 records from now until you press it again and saves the clip, whether or not replay is on. it pauses automatically when you turn on span, mirror or wallpaper. turning on spout or ndi output pauses the background replay recorder so the live feed stays smooth. press f9 again after the show if you want the replay back. in stage, the capture bank records 8, 16 or 32 bar loops locked to the live tempo. export settings in setup, output , beside the replay switch: export quality social (1080p at 60 frames per second, sized for social platforms) or master (the native render resolution and a much higher bitrate, for editing); export format mp4 (h.264 and aac, the one container instagram, tiktok and x all accept) or webm (vp9 and opus, encoded in software, so slower); recording dynamic range sdr, sdr 10 bit, hdr pq or hdr hlg; and the recording watermark switch. changing quality, format or range restarts the replay buffer. tier note f9 replay, shift+f9 recording and loop export are free for everyone, with a watermark on the clip; turning the watermark off is a studio feature. adding and playing video loops ships in the studio tier, which is not on steam yet; browsing the loop library is open at every tier. see pricing . the steam page is authoritative. ← previous wallpaper + displays next → lyrics

title: Lyrics
desc: Synced lyrics on screen, where they come from, and what to do when a track has none.
text: user guide / lyrics lyrics synced lyrics on screen, where they come from, and what to do when a track has none. lyrics words on the show synced lyrics ride the visuals, line by line, timed to the track. click the album art on the console to open them; click again to put them away. three modes classic draws the current line clean over the show. physics hands each line to a physics simulation, so words drift, swing, and settle with their own weight. the third button, native , shows lines the same way classic does. make them yours position the line at the top, center, or bottom of the stage, scale the font from subtle to headline, set the opacity, and pick a color: the theme accent, white, or a swatch of your own. where the words come from ikandy reads lyrics from your own files, matched by the artist and title of the playing track: a synced .lrc file saved next to the track, or one in your linked lyrics folder. synced files scroll in time with the music; plain text shows as static lyrics. if no local file matches, ikandy shows nothing instead of guessing, which is where the next part comes in. add your own: tap to time open add lyrics and paste the words. if they already carry timestamps, they play immediately. if they are plain text, tap to time turns timing them into a performance: play the track and stamp each line the moment it lands. seekable sources get a small timeline with previous, play, and next, so a missed stamp is a two-second fix, not a restart. saved lyrics live in your local lyrics folder, keyed by title and artist, and you can point ikandy at a folder of your own. on the broadcast lyrics have their own broadcast switch: show them on the second screen, spout, and recordings , or keep the output clean. tier note lyrics ship in the pro tier, physics mode and the tap-to-time editor included; see pricing . the steam page is authoritative. ← previous loops + recording next → stage: perform

title: STAGE: perform
desc: Now/Next decks, GO with crossfades, blackout and strobe, pads, rundowns, shows, combos.
text: user guide / stage: perform stage: perform now/next decks, go with crossfades, blackout and strobe, pads, rundowns, shows, combos. the console you perform from stage is the live view: a broadcast desk for planning a night and steering it in real time. when stage is live, the main window shows a return button so you always know which surface has control. now, next, go two decks with live previews: now is what the room sees, next is what you have lined up. click next to pick a look from the library, long-press to grab whatever is currently playing, right-click to clear. hit go and next takes the stage with a real crossfade: the outgoing frame freezes and dissolves into the incoming look, so transitions read as intentional, never as a cut. hold pins the current look against the autopilot. ride the moment a row of momentary performance keys sits under your fingers: blackout , a beat-locked strobe , and freeze . flash, strobe and the return from blackout share one limit of three flashes a second, for everyone: a flash pressed too soon waits for its turn, and at very fast tempos strobe skips a beat. press and hold; release and the show returns. every stage control carries an address, so all of it lands on midi and osc . pads hot-cue pads hold looks you want on a trigger, each with a live thumbnail. assign a pad, hit it when the room needs it. rundowns, plans, pools, autopilot build a rundown for the night: concrete entries play a specific look with its own duration, pool entries shuffle from a group you curated. reorder by drag; unset entries flag themselves so nothing surprises you mid-set. autopilot follows the rundown, or smart-shuffles when none is loaded, with a dwell you pick from seconds to minutes and a live countdown to the next switch. shows new / save / duplicate manage whole shows: click a saved show to load it, or its × to delete it. a saved show carries the rundown, your pads, and the per-output setup, so friday's rig comes back with one click. mix the mix tab is a layer compositor with a live preview: stack looks into a composite, save it, and recall the whole stack in one click. tempo and the logo tap four or more times to set the bpm by feel; double-click to clear it. the logo button opens the image studio to build or edit your overlay and lights up whenever one is live. outputs route per screen, so the projector and the stream can carry different dressing. stage ships in the studio tier. tier contents at launch are listed on the pricing page ; the steam page is authoritative. ← previous lyrics next → logo maker

title: Logo maker
desc: Image Studio: text or image, a rack of live treatments, live on any visual.
text: user guide / logo maker logo maker image studio: text or image, a rack of live treatments, live on any visual. image studio: make the logo the logo maker builds a broadcast-style overlay that rides on top of any running visual: your name, your mark, live on the output. create start from text or bring an image from your library. a studio preview backdrop helps you judge it, and it is preview only: your logo stays transparent and the backdrop is never baked into the asset. treatments a rack of live treatments ships today, and you can stack them: liquid metal , spectral film , chromatic map , sculpted relief , dimensional extrude , precision trace and more. several answer the music on their own controls, so the logo can breathe with it or hold still. save and apply apply live puts it on the output immediately. save as new keeps a version; originals and templates are protected from overwrite. on stage, the logo button opens the studio directly and lights up whenever an overlay is live, so you always know it is on. ← previous stage: perform next → midi, phone remote, gamepad

title: MIDI, phone remote, gamepad
desc: Bind hardware with MIDI Learn, steer from your phone over LAN, fly with a controller.
text: user guide / midi, phone remote, gamepad midi, phone remote, gamepad bind hardware with midi learn, steer from your phone over lan, fly with a controller. hands on the rig three ways to drive ikandy without touching the mouse: hardware midi, your phone, and a game controller. midi learn click midi learn , then move a control on your hardware. that knob or fader is now bound. bindings can be exported and imported as json, so a rig setup travels with you. bound controls tick green so you can see the mapping land. osc stage carries an osc receiver: switch it on, set the port, and send. every stage control has a stable address (strobe, blackout, go, pads, and the rest), so lighting desks and show controllers speak to ikandy the same way your hardware does. phone remote (lan) start the phone remote and a phone on your local network can steer the show from its browser once it enters the pairing code shown on screen; new code makes a fresh one. it is meant for a private network, not the internet: control traffic is not encrypted, so avoid venue guest wi-fi. osc has its own source-ip allowlist for lan mode. gamepad flight flight scenes accept a controller with zero setup: plug one in and any input takes the controls. left stick steers, right stick looks, right trigger throttle, left trigger brake. hands off for five seconds and the autopilot resumes; tab or the controller’s lb button hands back instantly. the mouse never touches the camera, it belongs to the ui. midi and osc control ship in the studio tier. see pricing ; the steam page is authoritative. ← previous logo maker next → shader import + reactivity

title: Shader import + reactivity
desc: Paste a shader, drive it from the music. Three layers, in the order to reach for them: the knobs that already exist, your own knobs from one comment block, then the audio uniforms read straight from your code. None of it needs an AI key.
text: user guide / shader import + reactivity shader import + reactivity paste a shader, drive it from the music. three layers, in the order to reach for them: the knobs that already exist, your own knobs from one comment block, then the audio uniforms read straight from your code. none of it needs an ai key. layer one: the knobs you already have open the console. these act on whatever is on screen right now, imported shaders included, with no editing and no reload. bass 0 to 2 · starts at 1 a color knob: warms the body of the picture. it never changes what your shader hears or how it moves. mid 0 to 2 · starts at 1 a color knob: shifts the picture’s colors like oil on water. treble 0 to 2 · starts at 1 a color knob: lights the edges. smooth 0.30 to 0.98 · starts at 0.30 higher glides, lower twitches. one global analyser setting. intensity 1 to 11 · starts at 8 the big fader. multiplies all three bands your shader reads. speed 0.1 to 2 · starts at 1 scales the scene clock for imported glsl. never touches the music. only one of them scales what your shader hears, and that is the part most people miss: what your shader actually receives u_bass = rawbass × intensity (0 to 2) the intensity fader reads 1 to 11 on screen but drives 0 to 2 underneath: display 6 is 1.0× , display 11 is 2.0× , and the default display 8 is 1.4× . a factory-fresh ikandy is already feeding your shader 1.4 times what it was written for. want more? intensity at 11 gives you 2× the raw band, about 1.4 times the default. that is the ceiling from the console alone. want it dead still? intensity at 1 sends every band to exactly zero. that is deliberate: it is the defeat switch, not a low setting. every console knob is one setting for every scene and every engine. bass, mid and treble color the finished picture; they never move your shader or change what it hears. the reactivity section all three of its knobs act on an imported shader, and motion beside them opens the motion window (pro and studio): light-sync (starts at 75%) lets the beat drive brightness and glow in the post chain. fx pulse (starts at 50%) lets hits pump the bloom, chromatic aberration and vignette for a moment. motion warp starts at 2.0×: the song’s sections set your shader’s own pace, quicker in a drop and slower in a breakdown, never faster on each bass note. 0 is off. see color, zoom, and the motion rule . layer two: your own knobs, one comment block put a single line comment in your pasted source and ikandy builds you real knobs in the console's scene section: sliders, toggles, dropdowns, a proper color picker. they persist with the scene and come back when it reloads. // ikandy-controls: [ // {"id":"glow", "label":"glow", "type":"float", "range":[0,2], "default":0.8, "mapsto":"u_glow"}, // {"id":"tint", "label":"tint", "type":"color", "default":"#66ccff", "mapsto":"u_tint"}, // {"id":"spin", "label":"spin", "type":"bool", "default":true, "mapsto":"u_spin"} // ] void mainimage(out vec4 fragcolor, in vec2 fragcoord) { vec2 uv = fragcoord / iresolution.xy; vec3 col = u_tint * smoothstep(0.8, 0.0, length(uv - 0.5)); col *= 1.0 + u_glow * u_basss; // your knob, times the music fragcolor = vec4(col, 1.0); } put it anywhere in the pasted source. on a multipass shader it goes in the common tab, or the top of image if you have no common tab, and every pass can read the uniform. four rules that will bite you do not declare the uniform yourself. ikandy writes uniform float u_glow; for you. adding your own is a redefinition error, and you get a message telling you to delete the line. read it or lose it. a control that is declared but never actually read in the code is dropped, and the load status names it. no dead knobs. reading it inside a comment does not count, because comments are stripped before the check. one block per shader. a second block is an error, not a merge. a malformed block stops the load and tells you the block line and the source line. it never quietly gives you zero knobs. fields field needed what it does mapsto yes the uniform name: u_ plus letters, digits, underscore. cannot be a built-in like u_bass . label should the name on the knob. type should float (knob, the default), int , color (picker, arrives as a vec3), bool (toggle), enum (dropdown, needs options ). range float / int [min, max] default should starting value. colors take "#rrggbb" or [r,g,b] in 0 to 1. id should short key used for saving. defaults to mapsto . options enum [{"value":0,"label":"soft"}, ...] audiodefault no wires the knob to a band. see below. up to 12 controls. duplicate or reserved mapsto names are dropped, with the reason logged to the developer console. in a wgsl import you read uc.glow inside fs_main , which is your mapsto with the u_ prefix removed. everything else is identical. point a knob at a band this is the direct answer to “how do i put the bass on something else?” add audiodefault to any float or int control and that knob is modulated by the band every frame, without touching your shader code. // ikandy-controls: [ // {"id":"glow", "label":"glow", "type":"float", "range":[0,2], "default":0.8, // "mapsto":"u_glow", "audiodefault" : {"band": "bass" , "gain":1.5}}, // // {"id":"hue", "label":"hue", "type":"float", "range":[0,1], "default":0.2, // "mapsto":"u_hue", "audiodefault" : {"band": "treble" , "gain":0.6}} // ] how the value is computed each frame value = knob position × (1 + band × gain) bands are bass , mid , treble and volume . gain is clamped to 0 to 8. the knob you set by hand stays the base, so you keep a manual trim on top of the music. bands are for light and color. a knob that moves the picture does not follow a band, whatever you pick: a speed knob keeps the value you set, and a camera, zoom, field of view, distance, scale or size knob gets a short punch on the beat instead, at most 1.5 percent of its value. repointing it live, without editing you can move a control from one band to another while the shader runs: load the shader, then save it. reopen it from the my scenes dropdown with open , in the same panel. every float and int control now shows a small pill under its name: off, bass, mid, treble, volume. pick one. it applies immediately and is remembered. the pill appears only on a shader the panel itself opened, which is why the save-then-open step matters. loading a fresh paste gives you the knobs but not the pills. one more thing worth knowing: if you later edit the ikandy-controls block in the saved file, the file wins over the remembered pill settings on the next load. layer three: straight into the source the fastest loop. the paste box is the editor: type in it and press ctrl+enter to recompile. ikandy declares all of these for you, so just read them. uniform what it carries u_bass u_mid u_treble the three bands, after your console knobs and intensity. fast and spiky. u_basss u_mids u_trebs the same bands, envelope-smoothed. use these for anything that should glide. u_kicktight the kick drum transient, 50 to 110 hz. the structural pulse. u_snare backbeat body and crack. good for color and saturation flares. u_hihat 6 to 16 khz tick. fast, fine sparkle. u_subbass 20 to 60 hz rumble. slow glow and depth. u_air 16 to 22 khz sheen. slow shimmer. u_basshit u_midhit u_trebhit raw onset envelopes per band. u_buildup u_peak u_calm u_release u_sustain u_arc song shape. these rise and fall over seconds, not beats. stage the drop with them. u_beat u_beatphase u_barphase u_bpm the live beat clock. u_mcimpact u_mcdrop u_mcrecoil u_mcfollow u_mcturn and more the motion conductor: twenty channels, from hits on the predicted beat to builds and drops. movement belongs on the small recoil, follow and turn channels; the rest drive light and staging. u_drive the intensity fader itself, 0 to 2. multiply your reactivity by it so your shader goes fully still at zero. u_volume u_intensity overall loudness. u_volume is the rms of the bands, u_intensity is their mean. spectrumat(x) waveformat(x) helper functions. sample the full spectrum or waveform; x and the result are both 0 to 1. shadertoy shaders work unchanged. every ichannel resolves to ikandy's live audio in the exact 512×2 texture format shadertoy uses: fft on one row, waveform on the other. a shader that already samples a music channel reacts the moment it loads, with nothing to press. iresolution , imouse , idate , iframe and the rest are wired too. shadertoy library textures do not travel with an export, so bind your own image or the shader renders without them. the one real craft rule. give each instrument its own job: kick drives one thing, snare another, hats another. that separation is the difference between a shader that pumps and a shader that just brightens all over. driving everything from u_bass is the most common reason an import looks flat. color, zoom, and the motion rule color, brightness, glow, sparkle, saturation and contrast are open season. drive any of it from any signal, as hard as you like. zoom, camera and whole-frame motion are different. your hand-written shader can do it, because a fresh paste renders exactly as written and nothing rewrites your code. ikandy’s own tools keep music-driven movement small and on the beat, and that is a decision rather than an oversight: motion on the beat lives in the motion window : swell, bounce, punch, drift and speaker move the finished picture on every scene, imports included, within set limits, and intensity 0 stops them. swell on the hit and a slow drift are on from the start on every plan; the motion window is pro and studio. motion warp on the console ships at 2.0× and only changes your shader’s clock speed, following the song’s sections, never each bass note. the basic button injects brightness, warmth and glow only. it used to warp time; that was removed. ignite , the ai path for imports, never ties a band level to camera, zoom or geometry. ai create may use only the motion conductor’s small, capped moves (a short recoil, follow or turn on a hit), and every scene it makes is checked for that before it is accepted. the reason is motion comfort. repetitive whole-field movement in roughly the 0.08 to 0.5 hz band is what makes people queasy, and music sitting at 100 to 140 bpm puts a bass-driven zoom uncomfortably close to it. drift, on from the start, already gives the picture a slow glide and zoom that follows the song. if you want more breathing zoom, write it yourself, keep the amplitude small, and watch it on a big screen for a few minutes before you put it in front of a room. two things people ask does an ai key change any of this? no. every layer above is free of provider cost and works offline. a key buys three things: ignite , which reads a non-reactive shader and proposes audio bindings for you to review before anything applies; tune , which looks at the running frame and balances the gains; and ai create , which writes whole scenes from a prompt. if you already write your own reactivity, a key mostly buys you the gain-balancing pass. see ai scene generation . can i build .milk presets in ikandy? not today. ikandy reads them very well: drop a folder of .milk files and they convert in the app, get security-screened, and land in rotation, tested with ten thousand presets at once. but nothing in the app writes a .milk file, so authoring still needs milkdrop itself or a preset editor. see visualizers + presets . shader import ships in the pro tier, alongside the ai shader studio. see pricing ; the steam page is authoritative. accurate as of ikandy 1.7. ← previous midi, phone remote, gamepad next → ai scene generation

title: AI scene generation
desc: Bring your own key. Generate, fix, and tune scenes with a supported provider.
text: user guide / ai scene generation ai scene generation bring your own key. generate, fix, and tune scenes with a supported provider. an ai that writes scenes ikandy can generate new visual scenes with ai, and can repair or tune imported shaders in the ai shader studio. it is bring-your-own-key: you connect an account from a supported provider and pay that provider directly. ikandy does not sell separate ai credits. your key stays yours the credential is stored using the operating system's secure storage. ikandy uses it to authenticate requests to the provider you choose; provider terms and data handling apply. what it can do generate : describe a look and get a runnable scene. ai fix : paste a shader that will not compile and let the sandbox suggest a repair after a compile check. ai tune : on a running scene, it looks at the current frame and suggests new bass, mid, treble and overall levels; you see a before and after and approve or reject the numbers. ignite : reads an imported shader that does not react to music yet and proposes the audio bindings that make it react, for you to review before anything applies. costs provider charges, availability, and estimates can change. review the estimate shown in ikandy and your provider's terms before you submit a job. guided ai scene generation ships in the pro tier. see pricing ; the steam page is authoritative. ← previous shader import + reactivity next → steam workshop

title: Steam Workshop
desc: Publish scenes you made, pull in what other players made, and keep your name on the work.
text: user guide / steam workshop steam workshop publish scenes you made, pull in what other players made, and keep your name on the work. the workshop shelf the library's workshop shelf browses everything the community has published, straight from the steam workshop, without leaving the app. browse and download open the library and choose workshop on the rail. search, filter by everything,
